newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends narrowly weaker, resists contango.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends narrowly weaker, resists contango.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended lower on Tuesday, extending the week's losses to 62 cents but resisting unrelenting pressure from amply supplied physical markets to dip into contango, dealers said.
April Brent, which expires on Friday, shed four cents to close at $19.24 a barrel, just four cents off the intraday high. The April/May spread closed virtually unchanged at +14 cents.

Brent staged a recovery off late afternoon lows as dealers took profits on short positions but expectations of a further rise in U.S. crude stocks when the American Petroleum Institute (API) reports later on Tuesday kept the underlying tone weak.
"There should be a build and that will give the market another good kick," said a broker.
Dealers said a big rise in U.S. inventories could signal the start of another major move to the downside. The March 3 low of $18.68 would be the first target.
"Once we see a sustained break below the $19 level on the front month then we're out of the new range and back to the bad old range," said a broker.
Traders said the weight of unsold March cargoes of North Sea and West African crudes was exacting a heavy toll on spot market differentials.

European oil inventory data released on Tuesday contributed to the bearish sentiment, as middle distillate stocks jumped by 7.13 million barrels in February and gasoline stocks rose 1.45 million barrels.
Earlier, IPE March gas oil futures closed down $3.75 at $163.25 a tonne, in line with weaker Brent crude and NYMEX product prices.
The March/April spread was stable in a $2 contango, with April settling at $165.25 a tonne.
